title: U.S. House · Georgia's 2nd Congressional District
area: Southwest Georgia, including Columbus and Albany.

context.text: Incumbent Sanford Bishop Jr. (D), who has represented the district since 1993, advanced unopposed from the Democratic primary. Matt Day won the Republican primary unopposed after A. Wayne Johnson and Chuck Hand did not make the ballot. Brandon Daley is also running, on the Communist Party line.

candidates.name: Sanford Bishop Jr.
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Democratic primary unopposed.
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for Georgia's 2nd Congressional District (since 1993)

summary.text: Sanford Bishop Jr. is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Georgia's 2nd Congressional District, first elected in 1992. He is a lawyer and former state legislator seeking re-election.

background.text: Born in Mobile, Alabama, in 1947; earned a bachelor's degree from Morehouse College in 1968 and a J.D. from Emory University in 1971; worked as a lawyer.
Served in the Georgia House of Representatives from 1977 to 1990 and the Georgia Senate from 1992 to 1993 before being elected to Congress.

priorities.text: Says he supports federal investments in infrastructure and transportation networks as fundamental to quality of life and the region's economy.

As a senior member of the Appropriations Committee, says he supports a responsible federal budget that funds programs that affect Americans' lives while drawing revenue from a tax code that is fair, balanced, and fiscally responsible.
Says ensuring veterans and their families are cared for after their service is a priority.

positions.summary: Says he strongly supports the Second Amendment, while also saying it is appropriately subject to reasonable, commonsense measures including background checks to limit access by those whose mental health or criminal history shows a lack of responsibility.
positions.quote: The Second Amendment to the United States Constitution, which Congressman Bishop strongly supports, is appropriately subject to reasonable, commonsense measures, including background checks to limit access by those whose mental health or criminal history demonstrates a lack of requisite responsibility.

positions.summary: Says immigration reform must strengthen border security by increasing law-enforcement manpower and providing the tools to enforce existing immigration laws and punish offenders.
positions.quote: Any immigration reform must include provisions that strengthen border security by increasing law enforcement manpower, utilizing new technology and fencing, and providing the tools, resources, and infrastructure necessary to enforce existing immigration laws and punish offenders.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Appropriations, including the Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug Administration and Related Agencies; Financial Services and General Government; and Military Construction, Veterans Affairs and Related Agencies subcommittees, in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).
